instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the beef and cook for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until it's no longer pink.
Add the onions, finely chopped, and cook for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, finely chopped, and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the salt, paprika and pepper.
Transfer the filling to a bowl and let it cool for 15 minutes. Hot filling will tear the pastry.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Melt the butter in the microwave or a small pan. Brush a 9 by 13 inch baking dish with half of it.
In a bowl, whisk the egg, then whisk in the vegetable oil, milk, yogurt and vinegar.
Lay one yufka sheet in the dish, folding the edges in so it fits. Brush it with a third of the egg mixture.
Spread the cooled filling over it in an even layer.
Lay the second sheet over the filling and brush it with another third of the egg mixture. Lay the third sheet on top.
Stir the rest of the melted butter into the last of the egg mixture. Brush it over the top sheet and sprinkle on the sesame seeds.
Cut the borek into 12 squares with a sharp knife, cutting all the way through.
Bake for 45 minutes, until it's golden brown and crisp on top.
Let it rest for 5 minutes, then serve the squares warm.

Let the leftovers cool completely. The squares keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days. To freeze, wrap the squares well. They keep in the freezer for up to 3 months. Reheat from the fridge in a 350°F (180°C) oven for 10 minutes, or from frozen wrapped in foil for 15 minutes.
method_notes: Both sources agree on a beef and onion filling seasoned with salt, pepper and paprika, and a whisked egg, oil, milk, yogurt and vinegar mixture brushed on the yufka. The lead folds small parcels; the second source gives the tray version used here, with sauce between the sheets, cut into squares before baking. Storage times come from the lead, which freezes the unbaked parcels; freezing the baked squares is the same idea but not tested in either source. Filo can replace yufka. Honest time is 75 minutes, a batch dish for days.
